rows.evidence_quote: Geostationary Lightning Mapper (GLM) Combined Monthly Thunder Hour data (https://dx.doi.org/10.5067/GLM/DATA301)

supporting_quotes.quote: Network (ENTLN), Global Lightning Dataset (GLD360), and World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN).
consists of daily files containing hourly maps of Thunder Hours.
Following DiGangi et al. (2022), a thunder hour is assigned to any grid box within 15 km of two or more GLM group centroids during that hour.
The GLM Combined Monthly Thunder Hours Data are one of several thunder hour datasets that GHRC will be archiving.

rows.keyword_priority_note: The companion product's User Guide lists glmmth by DOI under 'Related Data' (product list = priority 1); Step 4 confirms the DOI.
rows.decision_procedure: Q1-Q2 no: neither document says glmmth is made from glmhth files. Q3 no. Q4 yes: both are written from the same artifact-filtered GLM group data with the same thunder-hour definition, one hourly and one monthly -> parallel_product (RELATED).
rows.mapping_note: A monthly sum of the hourly product is plausible ('Monthly summed thunder hours') but undocumented; kept RELATED (rule 1c-6). glmmth's own guide doesn't name glmhth.
rows.confidence_rule: HIGH rule: source, statement and CMR validation all strong

rows.evidence_quote: World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN) Monthly Thunder Hour data (https://dx.doi.org/10.5067/WWLLN/DATA101)

supporting_quotes.quote: Thunder hours are the number of hours in a given month during which at least two WWLLN strokes were observed within 15 km of each grid point.
The GLM Combined Monthly Thunder Hours Data are one of several thunder hour datasets that GHRC will be archiving.

rows.keyword_priority_note: glmmth's User Guide cites it by DOI under 'Related Data'; Step 4 confirms the DOI.
rows.decision_procedure: Q1-Q4 no (no data flows between them). Q5 yes: the same monthly thunder-hour product (0.05 deg, 15 km rule) from another lightning observing system (ground-based WWLLN) -> equivalent_product (RELATED).
rows.mapping_note: WWLLN strokes are also used to screen GLM artifacts, but that input is the WWLLN stroke data (not a CMR collection), not wwllnmth.
rows.confidence_rule: HIGH rule: source, statement and CMR validation all strong
